neighbours.label: the verb slot right after a modal: 'be' after would/can/may/could, and 'to' after 'would/will have'
fire: Everyone agreed it would be a mistake to sell the farm now.
He realised he would have to work two jobs to pay the rent.
Officials say there can be no excuse for such long delays.
These photographs may be reproduced for classroom use only.
The mayor admitted that it would be difficult to finish the bridge on time.
Analysts warned that the company would have to cut costs sharply.
Critics argue the new rule could be challenged in court.
Fans know the team will have to play much better on Sunday.
quiet: Everyone agreed that selling the farm now was a mistake.
He worked two jobs last year to pay the rent on time.
Officials apologised for the long delays at the station.
These photographs were taken for a classroom project in 1990.
The mayor admitted the bridge was behind schedule again.
Analysts said the company cut costs sharply last quarter.
Critics challenged the new rule in court last month.
Fans saw the team play much better on Sunday.

notes: Probe: 'would have to' 0.59, 'quisiera' 0.44, 'can be no' 0.44, 'would be' 0.36, 'may be' 0.25. 'were able to' 0.02, 'must not' 0.02, 'bee' 0.01, 'has two' 0.04. So it is modal + be/have-to, not 'to' or 'able' in general. Near misses state the same facts without a modal.
